title: How the day closed
text: Friday was a very hard day for stocks. All 17 names on our list closed lower, and the S&P 500 fund SPY fell 3.6% while the tech heavy QQQ fell 5.5%. The biggest drops were in AI chip makers: NVIDIA fell 14%, AMD 13% and Broadcom 12%. The calmest names were Eli Lilly (down 0.2%), the dividend fund SCHD (down 0.7%) and Lockheed Martin (down 1.1%). Days like this show why spreading money across different kinds of companies matters.

title: NVIDIA drops 14% and sits at its 52 week low
text: NVIDIA closed at $125.53, right at the bottom of its range for the past year. A news report said the SEC, the government's market referee, is looking into its accounting. It was the stock's seventh losing day in a row. Our risk score for NVIDIA rose from 6.2 to 6.7, which moves it from Medium to High risk.

title: AI chip makers fell much more than AI giants
text: Companies that make the parts for AI (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC and Vertiv) fell between 9% and 14%. The big AI users like Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon fell only 3% to 4%. This shows that chip makers usually swing more than the large companies that buy their chips.

title: Alphabet also touches its yearly low
text: Alphabet (Google) fell 2.7% to $265.29, close to its lowest price of the past 52 weeks. Analysts' average price target is about $403, roughly 52% higher. A price target is only a guess, so it can be wrong, especially in a nervous market.

title: Rocket Lab and Vertiv keep the highest risk scores
text: Rocket Lab fell 10.9% and Vertiv fell 10.1%. Rocket Lab is now about 70% below its high of the year, and its risk score stays at the top of our scale, 10 out of 10. Big swings both ways are normal for these stocks.

title: Lesson 61: What is the SEC?
text: The SEC is the Securities and Exchange Commission. It is a U.S. government agency that acts like a referee for the stock market. Its job is to make sure companies tell investors the truth about their money, so people can make fair decisions. When the SEC has questions, it can open an investigation, which means it asks for documents and looks closely at the facts. An investigation is not a finding that someone did something wrong; many end with no penalty. Still, the news can make a stock fall, because investors dislike uncertainty. That is what happened to NVIDIA on Friday after a news report said the SEC is looking at its accounting.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices are from Friday's close (November 20, 2026) for all 17 names.
